title: Void functions (non-value returning functions)
recap: A void function performs an action without sending a data value to its caller. Reaching its closing brace is enough to resume execution in the caller, so an empty return at the end adds no useful behavior.
Call a void function as a complete statement when its behavior is what matters. It cannot stand where an expression requires a value, even when the function itself writes visible text to the console.
objectives: Use void for functions whose purpose is an action rather than a computed result.
Invoke void functions as standalone statements.
Distinguish console output from a function return value.
Allow a void function to finish naturally at its closing brace.
warnings: A void call cannot be inserted into an output or arithmetic expression that needs a value.
Returning a value from a void function is a compilation error.
An empty return at the end of a void function is redundant.
challenge: Complete the four functions in this order. 1. In printTagHeader(), use std::cout to write exactly `SAFETY TAG` followed by a newline. 2. In printHarnessStatus(), use std::cout to write exactly `Harness: inspected` followed by a newline. 3. In printTagFooter(), use std::cout to write exactly `Status: ready` followed by a newline. 4. In main(), keep the calls in header, harness, footer order and return 0. Keep all three printing functions void and parameterless, do not add a return statement to them, do not write directly from main(), qualify cout with std::, and do not add `using namespace std;`.
hints: First complete printTagHeader(): find its TODO and make that function write the exact heading with std::cout and a newline, without adding a return statement.

Language-neutral pseudocode: PRINT_TAG_HEADER: OUTPUT `SAFETY TAG`; PRINT_HARNESS_STATUS: OUTPUT `Harness: inspected`; PRINT_TAG_FOOTER: OUTPUT `Status: ready`; MAIN: CALL PRINT_TAG_HEADER, CALL PRINT_HARNESS_STATUS, CALL PRINT_TAG_FOOTER, RETURN success.

Near-C++ structure: `void printTagHeader() { <write heading> }`, `void printHarnessStatus() { <write harness status> }`, and `void printTagFooter() { <write readiness status> }`. Keep `int main()` as three standalone calls followed by its existing success return; use `std::cout` only inside the void functions.
